quick_english: Now the rite described by Shiva is set forth for attaining disciplehood: when a teacher wishes to appoint one established in the vow into disciplehood, guruhood, or adept-hood.

By the count of six, eight, and double twenty-four, the five-wheel system is called in the scripture named Shri-prior.
Thirty-two and its double, in the Shri-mat-Traishira view, and the connection with countless wheels, are described in the Shri-Siddha beginning.
Therefore, as the sacrifice is measured by the wheel, one should worship accordingly; by that, here one should draw three tridents.
In the three tridents, the three goddesses, by rotational course and by middle-left-right distinction, should become fully worshipped.
Maintenance before the mandala will be taught briefly: having drawn the mandala, one wipes it with scented cloth.
Having bathed, the guru, before the mandala here, should worship the external deities and the door deities at the door place.
In the front part of the mandala, from the northeast direction in order up to the southeast, one should fully worship Ganesha and the others up to the field protectors.
Ganapati, guru, Parama, Paramesthi, and the prior-siddha speech-field-lord, thus seven are named in the guru-row rite to be fully worshipped by our gurus.
Then, having taken command, the support power and related deities, worshipped with flowers, incense, and so forth, are sufficient from the trident root onward.
Up to Shiva, at the end of the white lotus, among the three tridents in order, true being should be in the middle trident together with the supreme.
On the left, together with another, the nine-souled one is right-going and supreme; on the trident's right, standing on the middle peak, is Rati-crown.
May it be together with supreme and lower powers: on the right Bhairava abides supremely, on the left on the trident, standing in the middle, the nine-souled one with another.
May it be supreme, together with the supreme power, on the left side, and Bhairava; thus, when Shri Para Devi is established in the all-pervading state.
The sacrifice becomes fully complete from that seat alone; therefore even on one trident, in sacrifice, one should contemplate that established.
Not knowing the rite, knowing the procedure, thus spoken by Trishika; then in the middle, so on the right, on the left, on the peak, and everywhere.
One should worship as one self up to the world guardians' weapons, and as supreme; one should fully honor all deities.
The glorious lord, mother-presence, uninjured; then also by enjoyment sacrifice, the knowledge limb, the Bhairava octad.
The pair and wheel goddesses, in their own place, one should worship outside; world guardians with weapons, with sandal, flowers, drinks, and so on.
One should worship with supreme devotion, free from wealth-deceit; then of pot, weapon, vase, circle, place, self.
One should do investigation of five from nondual meditation; but those who do not find that nondual pervasion, Shiva-natured.
By mantra channel application, they enter the nondual path; having exited by their own right from the circle-dwelling, from the left.
Having entered by another and exited, in pot place, in pitcher, in fire place, and thus in order, until in one's own left.

Resting in the navel wheel with breath-rays, becoming supreme by one's own power, one should here wrap the living being with the living being.

With force, uproot from essence this karma-bound one who nourishes and completes all principles.

The filament of nectar from the heart lotus, taken by leftward circuit, melts the tissue by gaining ascent to the heart center.
Taking the pure moon essence, slightly red and yellow, into the breath-body that is like the tip of an elephant's trunk.

When, in a half-ghatika sequence, rest-yoga occurs amid blood and similar essence-flow movements, the mass is present.

Thus seventy kinds are declared by purifier difference; when initiation with these mantras occurs without purifying nyasa.
Then it is to be known seventyfold, devoid of birth and so on; the purifiable difference is then to be stated, and that too is told in brief.
Tattva is fourfold from differences of one, three, five, six, and thirty-six; path and likewise four egg groups are from five and one differences.
Thus the purifiable is tenfold; thirtyfold from the threefold rule of that; by purifiable-purifier difference, hundreds and twenty-one.
Here too, by nyasa union, in purifiable sound and action, one hundred twenty-one kinds, devoid of birth and so on, becomes.
Consisting of birth and so on, thus in hundredfold scripture, scripture would be seventy plus; that also from substance-knowledge difference.
Twofold; eighty-five would be hundreds plus eleven; from enjoyment-liberation inquiry twofold, that is declared.
Purification of both inauspicious and auspicious things makes enjoyment twofold, with distinction across three times.
Through one, two, or all powers, enjoyment becomes seven or eightfold, and guru-disciple order divides it twofold.
Because direct initiation depends on continuity between two, its result is full; disagreement brings ruin.
In indirect immortal initiation, the guru alone, by the glory of action and knowledge, leads the disciple to the desired abode.
When action and knowledge are undivided, their continuity is likewise; action is again divided because it is of that nature.
The holy Svachanda treatise says result differs by impression distinction for disciples and guru, even when action and the rest are undivided.
Variety exists in enjoyment because continuity between purifier and purified produces such variety, and variety is the life of distinction.
Thus the path purified by those same mouths is joined; wishing to enjoy some principle, he becomes enjoyer endowed with that power.
Here, if auspicious actions exist, enjoyment variegation is such; in action purification, variegation is otherwise.
Enjoyment is joined by immediate exit or by body, then by practice or at body's end; thus it is fourfold.
The previous eight-division is said to become thirty-two through yoga; liberation, though one, is the seed called convention.
For child and known quick death, devoid of power; for aged or powerful, aiming; purification is twofold by purification or non-purification.
Mahesha speaks a command in the glorious cave concerning the guru's duty when death is near.
Seeing a disciple afflicted by old age and disease, the guru should transfer him and place him in the supreme principle.
Thirty-five distinctions of the guru, or of guru and disciple, are declared; seventy arise from the stated twofold calculation.
Having destroyed those previously stated initiation distinctions, the guru speaks enumeration for attainment of practiced knowledge.
The stated number, increased by forty, should be divided by seventy, and one should calculate initiation distinctions.
Here five lakhs, ninety-seven thousand, and eight hundred initiation distinctions are given in the Malini Tantra.
Seventy-fold and thirty-fold groups, purification, one principle and beyond, attendants, six rites, and duties yield four distinctions.
That knowledge composed of substance, free from birth and endowed with that, is thirty-five-fold from the union of enjoyment and liberation.
Enjoyment is thirty-two-fold by auspicious, pure, impure, and time distinctions; liberation is threefold; duty distinctions are seventy.
Initiation is divided in many ways by distinctions of purifier and purified; without the purified, it is seventy-fold.
From collecting mantra limb distinctions and enumerating fifteen distinctions of the purified and principles, the count arises.
The distinctions cannot be fully enumerated; unmixed distinctions exist, while mixed ones are many-fold.
Because purifier and purified distinctions exist, much remains to be done in enjoyment and accomplishment by the wise one's support.
Greater cause for greater fruit is no wonder; in liberation distinction remains through firm latent habit.
Even a small action is worthy of refuge; the teacher says again, when wealth, place, time and so on are present, or in knowledge alone.
Even in liberation, a broad collection of action and knowledge must be done, because consciousness fluctuation is varied and unsteady, joined gradually.
In each thing, shiva-natured establishment necessarily occurs; this truth, extracted by me, is for the disciple.
Thus in gradual awareness even a fool becomes shiva-natured, seeing the fortunate teacher who bestows such gradual shiva grace.
Even a child approaches shiva state by nondifference view and devotion strength; although discriminating activity remains, initiation gives liberation at the body's end.
Scripture declares that although the lord speaks thus, firm latent impression remains joined; even in liberation distinction exists, born of small or great action, such as same-world status.
Thus some call that unfit; varied enjoyment only would be said, during the middle of life with residual impressions, with vow lapse and so on.
No obstacle net comes, because action abundance is not an obstacle for the liberation seeker; the person purified by seeded initiation is protected even in vow lapse and so on.
Liberation after enjoyment is not thus in seedless initiation; some think this fit, and scripture remembers that.
From transgressing the vow, O goddess, one becomes carnivorous for a hundred years.
Therefore, for a dull student, sequential action beginning with extraction of principles is fitting and extensive even for liberation, when it is capable of bestowing established Shiva-bhava.
But a guru always habituated in knowledge through meditation may, for the disciple's liberation, practice any means he wishes.
Thus, in the disciple's body, the path to be purified is placed as desired, and the purifying mantra is placed above according to the principles.
By the establishment of the two matrikas, the letter sequence told before is so placed for the purification of each principle.
Although the letter path is declared and to be purified, it is bound and maya-born; the purifier is another, Shiva-natured and supreme speech.
Sadyojyotis said in the commentary on Svayambhuva: indeed one sound is bound-natured, and another is Shiva-natured.
Therefore the fitting purifier-purified relation of that very letter is also said in the previous scripture; they embrace it thus.
Having placed the faces beginning with Sadyojata and the limbs beginning with heart, five each, six times, one should perform the thirty-six placement from earth.
By reversal of the higher and lower in earth, three steps arise; then from water to ego through the support of five and eight.
Five steps are in the three named principles of intellect, root, and male color; three and one are in the two impure times; and one is in the controller.
One step is said here in kala and maya; in order, five steps are in vidyesvara, sadashiva, and shiva.
Nineteen steps should be the higher-lower arrangement, with halves, ones, twos, and the moon-eye pair.

In the placement of the pure purifying mantra, by the goddess's glory, eighteen fingers measure one foot, while another foot has another measure.
From the fourth foot in the six-foot context, two measures called supreme and inferior are twelve and twelve, with another as before above the principles.
According to the intent of pure purifying mantra placement, the great god again declares a placement opposite to that principle-order placement.
In the partless, the foot is one syllable up to three in the earthly context; by such and so on, the principle-gone order placement is declared.
Again in the Mālinī Tantra, from the distinction of class and knowledge, the lord says the feet are in two ways and describes another kind of named placement.
Each is to be known as two fingers; there the first three feet are eight fingers, four, ten fingers thence beyond.
In two fingers there are two feet and other; six fingers thence beyond; and twelve fingers other, two in five fingers separate.
Two feet are four-jointed, and other two are two-jointed; thus the independent placement of the supreme-inferior goddess is called.
To show that the two knowledges are joined in the disciple's body by pervader-ness only, no separate placement was formed.
Thus in the placement of the purifying mantra, from its ray union the noose-net would dissolve, from the meditation power of the teacher.
In the principle to be purified, for all sources at the same time, from birth and enjoyment, at the destruction of action there would be liberation.
Wonderful with so many bodies of the atom, even for the enjoyer, the mind-connection is not clear, having universe union and separation.
By necessity, the mind's activity is only in the body; beyond that there is no continuity, because it is constructed through one mind and united senses.
Local activity and knowledge of the self occur there; that object-knowledge does not deserve continuity in other bodies.
When that mind's body activity certainly becomes pure through yoga, mantra, and rite, then the knower acts.
As pure mind sees quickly even when far, so in initiation of understanding there is seeing of those worlds.
When one wishes initiation free from birth and so on, then the plan 'I lift from this' is proper deliberation.
Even without purification, the purifier rite there by mantra performs the birth sequence free from element union.
In the single purifier rite excluding birth and so on, only that purifier container should be imagined.
In initiation by substance union, sesame, ghee, unbroken rice, and grains are offered by respective mantra for birth union and separation.
When knowledge initiation is done to the disciple, then intensely by that mantra speech force one sees from the non-conceptual.
Concept is indeed speech-composed; that reflective one is mantra-self, and reflection is pure and bondage-natured.
Because eternal beginningless boon shiva identity is constructed, by its union the teacher's concept may attain shivahood.
In shri sara shastra this is spoken by the supreme lord: comprehension of meaning is object-subject-formed.
That very mantra-power, spread out in the mantra continuum, is declared as mantra-power of reflection-nature.
Reflection is twofold and divides mantras by purity and impurity; this is said in the holy Pauṣkara, and Brahma, Vishnu, and others are egg-born.
The primary attached beings are sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic; through their impure reflection the teacher becomes absorbed in that.
Vaishnava and others are declared bound souls, not fit for the lord's rule; mantras standing on the pure path, such as Shiva-bhattaraka and others, are fit.
The teacher seen by holy Matanga and others is absorbed in that and is Shiva; but can independent speech union alone produce reflection?
From where before? If from reflection, from where? In determination, the first would give unwaveringness from the teacher.
If there is transmitted speech, it too comes from another teacher; in previous order, before, it is from the first teacher.
Speech is indeed transmitted and exists today also; let it be grasped, even if such speech by force is independent.
Reflection is imagined; that too is indeed that self, well-determined, like pot and jar; or if difference is determined, thus.
That also gives other imagination and is not to be regarded; with effort it is valued, as doing thus, clearly in the fitting of imagination.
Hand and transmitted speech, those two, how indeed are they mixed from word to another word? By that, learning is interrupted.
But from practice, that directly reflects wonderful narrative; its reflection rises, and ancient own reflection may shine.
Natural awareness sets the limit for conceptualization arising from mantra meaning.
Mantra is honored when difference is seen through prior knowledge forms.
Another concept is unnecessary because the mark belongs to that alone.
The mantra-tantra expert states the mark for awakening mantra meaning.
In absence of a mantra-meaning knower, the guru practices mantra identification.
One should make a guru when practice produces equal speech through meditation.
In complete equality there is no difference; purpose action follows.
By reason, one sees the same purpose action even from other speech.
The truthful speaker is Shiva, and what he says becomes mantra.
This is not the position of Abhinavagupta, whose self is offered to mantra.
A mantra-offered mind removes poison, and that mantra word is supreme.
The beautiful lover, purified by that, is satisfied in himself.
